audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may capitalize unusually large favorable contract-estimate revisions as recurring earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $168.373 million FY2025 net revenue increase, equal to 62.8% of the $268.3 million OE anchor; $138.9 million additional net revenue increase in H1 2026; profit and OE effects unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially inflates anchor OE and every projected year if favorable cumulative catch-up revenue is treated as recurring operating performance.
audit_findings.evidence: Changes in contract estimates on performance obligations satisfied or partially satisfied in previous periods resulted in net revenue increases of $ 168,373 , $ 135,344 and $ 58,827 for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, and are included in “Operating income” on the Consolidated Statements of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not yet a demonstrated OE error because the disclosed amounts are revenue revisions, not quantified profit or cash-flow adjustments, and large favorable revisions continued in 2026. Nevertheless, their scale relative to the anchor makes normalization reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level revenue, gross-profit and cash effects, including subsequent reversals and completion status, then rerun all scenarios using OE adjusted only for the portion demonstrated to be nonrecurring.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated cash-flow components belonging partly to noncontrolling owners
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.572 million FY2025 NCI income; $157.595 million of VIE cash at 2026-06-30, equal to 33.9% of the $464.451 million bridge cash; net correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Misstates OE through parent/consolidated mismatches in depreciation, capex and working capital, and may overstate the bridge by adding cash partly attributable to noncontrolling owners.
audit_findings.evidence: The equity held by the remaining owners and their portions of net income (loss) are reflected in stockholders’ equity on the Consolidated Balance Sheets line item “Noncontrolling interests” and in the Consolidated Statements of Operations line item “Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests,” respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied calculation basis demonstrates a perimeter mismatch. Its net direction is mixed because consolidated depreciation add-backs can raise OE while consolidated capex and working-capital deductions can lower it; adding all VIE cash creates a separate upward bias. The filed scales are large enough to affect the valuation materially, although the parent-only correction cannot be calculated from the record.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE component and bridge cash amount on a Sterling-common economic-interest basis using VIE-level cash flows, ownership percentages, distribution restrictions and NCI claims, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The RHB stake may be counted both in owner earnings and in the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.934 million FY2025 Sterling share of RHB pre-tax income, $23.803 million of FY2025 distributions, and $108.0 million stake add-back; exact duplication unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalizes RHB earnings or distributions within OE and then adds the RHB investment again in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, Sterling’s 50% portion of earnings is treated as income and increases the investment in unconsolidated subsidiary account.
audit_findings.explanation: The record demonstrates that RHB income and distributions entered Sterling's filed earnings and cash flow and that the valuation separately adds the stake. It does not show whether both items were purged from OE. The potentially embedded RHB income equals 5.9% of the OE anchor, before capitalization, so the possible double count is reasonably capable of materially affecting value.
audit_findings.action: Trace RHB equity income, basis-step-up amortization and distributions through each annual OE calculation; rerun with RHB fully excluded from OE while retaining the stake, or retain RHB cash generation and remove the corresponding stake add-back.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to omit a non-debt acquisition claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $63.909 million computed at 2026-06-30 from $57 million opening liabilities minus $7.767 million payments plus $4.976 million fair-value expense plus $9.7 million Stone Ridge earn-out; approximately $2.06 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Overstates the common-equity bridge by failing to deduct contingent acquisition consideration not already paid through OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our aggregate earn-out liabilities totaled approximately $57 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated, but the computed claim is only 1.7%, 1.3% and 1.2% of bear, base and bull equity value, respectively. Deducting it would reduce each scenario by about $2.06 per share and the base-derived buy-below price by about $1.44, without changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the exact earn-out liability at the valuation date and deduct any unpaid amount not already captured elsewhere in OE or the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The anchor and current capital structure span different portions of the CEC acquisition perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.915 million filed FY2025 pro-forma increase in parent net income, equal to 0.34% of the OE anchor; H1 2026 CEC operating income contribution was $37.5 million; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Uses an anchor containing only four months of CEC operations with a post-acquisition share count, cash balance and acquisition claims, potentially understating starting OE.
audit_findings.evidence: From the acquisition date of September 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025, revenue associated with the CEC Acquisition totaled approximately $ 170,400 and its pre-tax income was approximately $ 19,400 .
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but its materiality to OE is unresolved. Filed pro-forma net income shows only a $0.915 million FY2025 uplift, while subsequent CEC operating income is much larger; neither figure establishes full-year owner earnings after capex, working capital, interest, taxes and earn-outs.
audit_findings.action: Construct audited pro-forma FY2025 and post-acquisition trailing-twelve-month OE for CEC, including amortization, interest, taxes, maintenance capex, working capital and earn-out cash costs, and rerun the valuation with the unchanged current diluted share count.
